item.title: Food and the Brain - Eating for Brain Health and Concussion Recovery
item.itunes:title: Food and the Brain - Eating for Brain Health and Concussion Recovery
item.description:
What should you eat when you want a sharper brain—or when the brain is recovering from a concussion or other neurological stress?

In this episode of Dr. M Experienced, with Dr. David Musnick, Dr. M connects food with brain health, neuroinflammation, blood-sugar stability, mitochondria, the gut-brain connection, and neuronal membranes.

Topics include:

• Apigenin, parsley, and the balance between inflammatory M1 and repair-oriented M2 microglia • A parsley, wild-blueberry, and protein smoothie • Choline, omega-3 DHA, plasmalogens, and neuronal membranes • Nrf2-supportive broccoli sprouts, green tea, turmeric, and rosemary • Quercetin-rich capers, red onions, and apples • Protein, lower-mercury fish, vegetable diversity, fiber, and the microbiome • Advanced glycation end products, acrylamide, heavy metals, BPA, MSG, aspartame, and sugar • Ketogenic diets, intermittent fasting, and when they may not be appropriate

Dr. M explains why he may consider gluten-free, cow-dairy-free, or selective short-term elimination strategies in some concussion and neurological cases. These are not universal and should be individualized with an appropriate clinician.

item.title: The Brain on Fire - Neuroinflammation After Concussion
item.itunes:title: The Brain on Fire - Neuroinflammation After Concussion
item.description:
After a concussion, symptoms can improve before the brain has rebuilt its full reserve. What does that mean for reinjury risk, neuroinflammation, and recovery?

In this episode of Dr. M Experienced, with Dr. David Musnick, Dr. M explains brain reserve, glial cells, inflammatory and repair-oriented microglia, and research-informed factors he considers after concussion.

Topics include:

• Why brain reserve can differ across regions and why symptom relief does not always mean full recovery • Protecting a healing brain from reinjury • Astrocytes and the blood-brain barrier • Oligodendrocytes, myelin, and neural support • Pro-inflammatory M1 and repair-oriented M2 microglial activity • Sleep, luteolin, apigenin, vitamin D, omega-3 fats, curcumin, and Nrf2 signaling as research-informed considerations

item.title: Concussion - What Happens in the Brain
item.itunes:title: Concussion - What Happens in the Brain
item.description:
A concussion can affect far more than what appears on a routine scan. What actually happens in the brain, and why can symptoms persist even without a direct hit to the head?

In this episode of Dr. M Experienced, with Dr. David Musnick, Dr. M explains concussion and traumatic brain injury mechanisms and why care should go beyond ruling out a brain bleed and simply waiting.

Topics include:

• Structural injury, neural shearing, excitotoxicity, and neuroinflammation • Oxidative stress, hypoxia, and blood-brain barrier disruption • Brain autoimmunity, hormones, pituitary involvement, and vagus nerve dysfunction • Mitochondrial dysfunction, protein-folding abnormalities, neurogenesis, and synaptogenesis • Gut-microbiome changes after injury • Brain fog, headache, dizziness, emotional instability, fatigue, sleepiness, and brain-based fatigue • Why a concussion can occur without the head directly striking an object

item.title: Energy - Understanding Fatigue and Mitochondrial Health
item.itunes:title: Energy - Understanding Fatigue and Mitochondrial Health
item.description:

In this episode of Dr. M Experienced, with Dr. David Musnick, Dr. M takes a functional-medicine look at energy, fatigue, mitochondrial health, and the importance of investigating root causes.

Topics include:

• Sleep quality, sleep apnea, and inflammation • Viral reactivation, Lyme and co-infections, mold exposure, and heavy metals • Hormones, adrenal and thyroid function, and liver and kidney stress • Mitochondrial function and ATP production • Grounding, sleep, methylated B vitamins, magnesium, zinc, copper, and CoQ10 • NAD support, PQQ, and methylene blue as options to evaluate in an individualized clinical context

item.itunes:title: Electromagnetic Frequencies (EMF) - Practical Ways to Reduce Exposure

In this episode of Dr. M Experienced, with Dr. David Musnick, Dr. M discusses radio frequency, electromagnetic fields, electrical fields, the blood-brain barrier, sleep, and practical mitigation strategies.

item.title: Insomnia - Causes and Practical Sleep Strategies

item.description:

In this episode of Dr. M Experienced, with Dr. David Musnick, Dr. M explains common forms of insomnia and offers practical ways to improve sleep timing, light exposure, wind-down routines, and daytime habits.

item.description:

In this episode of Dr. M Experienced, with Dr. David Musnick, Dr. M builds on Part 1 with a practical discussion of testing, clinical red flags, and foundational brain-supportive habits.

Topics include:

• When the duration, frequency, or pattern of brain fog deserves closer evaluation • Systemic inflammation and the relationship between body and brain inflammation • Full Epstein-Barr virus panels, including VCA IgG and IgM, EBNA, and Early Antigen • Mold and mycotoxin testing when exposure history supports it • Homocysteine and other blood clues that may inform a workup • When progressive cognitive change or neurological red flags may make brain imaging appropriate • Sleep, exercise, food quality, EMF reduction, and toxin avoidance while root causes are being investigated

item.title: Brain Fog, Part 1 - Is Your Brain in a Fog?
item.itunes:title: Brain Fog, Part 1 - Is Your Brain in a Fog?
item.description:
What does brain fog actually feel like, and what may be happening beneath slow thinking, low mental energy, poor focus, memory slips, or trouble finding words?

In this episode of Dr. M Experienced, with Dr. David Musnick, Dr. M explains brain fog as a sign worth investigating rather than something to dismiss as a normal part of age or stress.

Topics include:

• How brain fog can affect thinking speed, focus, memory, language, and mental stamina • Brain inflammation, microglia, neurotransmitters, and oxygen delivery • Potential contributors including concussion, autoimmunity, blood-sugar swings, hormones, mold, infections, heavy metals, EMF exposure, medications, and excitotoxins • Why root-cause evaluation matters when symptoms persist or progress • Foundational habits involving sleep, movement, food quality, parsley and apigenin, EMF reduction, and toxin avoidance
